questions.question: You should check your motorcycle completely:

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, pick:

options.text: Shoes with long heels.
Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.
Shoes that cover your ankles.
Shoes made from thin materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Keep heels short so they don't catch on things. Tuck in laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is safe as long as no other vehicles are near you.
Can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you cannot hold the turn, you may drift into another lane or even off the road. Always use caution when turning.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Speed up on the throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently brake using the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake using the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and go straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you are sure which one it is.

questions.question: To lower your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Tell other drivers your intentions.
Not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Ride where it is hard for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers your intentions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to grip the handlebars better.
Not be worn because they make controls harder to use.
Be worn only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to grip the handlebars better.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: A pre-ride check usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough check before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Penalties for riding while impaired may include:

options.text: License suspension.
Fines.
Community service.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If convicted of impaired riding, you may face fines, license suspension, jail time, court costs, legal fees, higher insurance rates, and community service. Do not ride if you have been drinking.

questions.question: Which clothing item will not reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front.
Not use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle ahead, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: Riding alongside a car:

options.text: Is a good idea.
Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only a problem when the road is wet.
Makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot where they cannot see you. Also, the vehicle blocks your way to escape.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean the same way the rider leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way the rider leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the rider and lean as the rider leans. Sit as close to the rider as you can without crowding them, and hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs with road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is lots of traffic.
A dangerous place for riders.
Hard to understand.
Safer than open roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: A dangerous place for riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because they have the most chances for crashes between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: When it is clear that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only need to use a turn signal at a traffic light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Signals matter even if you do not see other vehicles. Other drivers may be nearby but out of your view.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on:

options.text: Dry pavement
Gravel
Snow
Leaves

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces make traction poor for tires. These include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers. All of these are more dangerous than dry pavement for riders.

questions.question: An easy way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag on the bike frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder as much as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: You can be easier to see by wearing bright, reflective clothes. Ride with your headlight on all the time. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: A motorcycle headlight:

options.text: Must be on at all times.
Must be on only between sunset and sunrise.
Does not have to be white.
Must be on only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be on at all times.
questions.explanation: Minnesota law requires that a motorcycle headlight be on at all times when you are riding.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Polyester
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Make sure other drivers can see you.
Hide your plans from other drivers.
Always ride within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: The body gets rid of almost ______ of alcohol per hour.

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink
questions.explanation: On average, the body eliminates about one drink of alcohol per hour.

questions.question: Before riding, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes rub against the steering.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need to be checked regularly?

options.text: The brakes
The fasteners
The tires
The paint

questions.correctAnswerText: The paint
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. A small mechanical problem on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Jacket
Boots
Gloves
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle ahead.
Wear dark clothing.
Only signal when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can safely ride based on how you feel.
Set a limit so you can still ride safely.
Not ride.
Not worry if you feel fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking alcohol. Any amount of alcohol can affect your riding ability.

questions.question: The best way to learn about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Read the owner's manual.
Read a general motorcycle book.
Ask someone with a different motorcycle.
Watch a motorcycle show on television.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually:

options.text: Made of leather.
Made of wool.
Not shaped for your hand.
Unsafe for riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided because other drivers see you.
Are only needed in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine. This helps you know what is behind you.
